reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: Cool-roof soiling is dominated by fine soot, organics and biofilm held by van der Waals and capillary forces, so charge dissipation changes the aged SR by at most ~0.01, i.e. ~1 % less roof heat flux and ~1 % on the envelope.
reviews.proxy_reason: The gain equals the assumed aged-loss change (0.16 vs 0.18); the electrostatic mechanism is not modelled at all.
key_assumption_issues: Aged reflectance loss is an input, not an outcome of the electrostatic physics
ATO NIR absorption lowers clean SR
killer_risks: No measurable soiling benefit for the relevant fine absorbing particles

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: A glaze over closed-cell scattering rows should keep a life-mean SR of ~0.84 on roofs (horizontal glazes still collect dust and droppings) with emittance ~0.92, i.e. ~27 % less roof heat flux than the repainted acrylic (life-mean ~0.70); applied to roofs and facades ~18 % of the envelope objective.
key_assumption_issues: Clean SR 0.90 of glazed multi-row closed cells not demonstrated; glaze-cell interfaces reduce scattering contrast
Life-mean aged loss 0.05 on horizontal roofs
killer_risks: Hail and impact crack the brittle glaze and open cells
Crazing from expansion mismatch over 7000 thermal cycles
Only factory panels: no retrofit on existing roofs; glare from the specular glaze
